:: JUDGMENT :

This petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act 1988 by the petitioner praying to award compensation of Rs. 50,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the accident caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle,
bearing registration No. KA-29-M- 9054, near Jairamdas Junction, Bengaluru City on 28.03.2021 at about 4.30 p.m.
Due to the accident the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
2. Prior to an accident he was hale and healthy and he was working as driver and earning a sum of Rs. 30,000/- p.m.
After the accident he was not able to perform his work.
Therefore he sustained loss of income from the date of accident.
Therefore the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
3. In response to the notice, respondent no. 1 and 2 have appeared through the counsel and filed written statements.
4. Respondent no.1 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and contended that the amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive and without any base.
Hence prayed for dismissal of the petition with exemplary cost.
5. Respondent no.2 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further it admitted the issuance of the policy and denied the occurrence of the accident.
Further it contended that the rider of motor cycle had no valid driving license to rider the motor cycle and not wearing the helmet at the time of accident.

Further it contended that the driver had no valid driving license to drive the vehicle at the time of accident and contended that the amount claimed by petitioner is highly exorbitant, excessive and without any base.
Hence prayed for dismissal of the petition with exemplary cost.
6. On the basis of rival pleadings of the parties, the following issues were framed.

1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident that occurred on 28.03.2021 at 4.30 p.m due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Toyota Qualis bearing Reg.No.KA-29- M-9054?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what extent and from whom?

The medical record officer by name Chethan Kumar and got marked 4 documents at Ex.P15 to Ex.P18.
The respondent no.2 got marked Ex.R1 by consent.
8. Heard arguments and perused the records.

9. After assessing the oral as well as documentary evidence my findings on the above Issues are as fallows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :

 :: REASONS ::
Issue No.1:-
10.
To prove the rash and negligent act of driving on the part of the driver of the Toyota bearing Reg.No.KN- 29-M-9054, the petitioner relied upon the his oral evidence and police records.
11. The Ex.P1 is the FIR along with complaint, Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar along with sketch, Ex.P5 is the IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the charge sheet.
12. By going through the above said police record it clearly discloses the occurrence of the accident and the identity of the Toyota Qualis.
The charge sheet also speaks that the driver of the Toyota Qualis drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the petitioner's motor cycle.
Due to the said impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Therefore this court is of the opinion that accident occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Toyota Qualis.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
Issue No.2:-
13. In this case petitioner has claimed total compensation of Rs. 24,00,000/- lakhs for the injuries sustained by him in an accident on various heads.

14. In the decision reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 (Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another) Division Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court has laid down on what grounds compensation is required to be awarded in personal injury case.

In para 6 of the said judgment their Lordships have demarcated the heads under which compensation is required to be considered which reads as here under:

The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary damages(Special damages) (i)Expenses relating to treatment,
hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) future medical expenses Nonpecuniary damages(General damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)

(vi) Loss of expectation of life(shortening of normal longevity)
15.

From going through the above said decision, it is clear that under the pecuniary damages expenses relating to the treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure are required to be considered with.
In the second head loss of earning and other gains of the injured person is required to be considered.
In the background of principles laid down by their Lordships in the above said decision we to consider the quantum of compensation for which the petitioner is entitled to.
16. LOSS OF INCOME -
It is the case of the petitioner that he has sustained permanent disability due to injury sustained in an accident.
In order to prove the same the petitioner relied on the evidence of PW2 and documents produced by him.

PW.2 deposed that the petitioner has sustained Left lateral condyle of the tibia and under gone surgery of ORIF with LCP on 29.03.2021.
17.

He further deposed that on examination the petitioner had healed scar over the left knee,
restricted left knee movements with wasting of the thigh muscles.
The petitioner has suffered the injuries to his leg.
The use of the leg place vital role in the driver job.
So the above mentioned difficulties certainly will effect the work of petitioner.
Therefore I assess the functional disability of petitioner at 13%.
18. It is the specific case of the petitioner that prior to the accident he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But he has not produced any document with regard to his income.

Therefore, the income of the petitioner is taken as Rs.15,000/- p.m.
19.

Furthermore, Hon'ble Supreme Court in a full bench decision reported in 2020 SCC ONLINE 752, (PAPPU DEO YADAV V.S NARESH KUMAR AND OTHERS) held that, even in case of permanent partial disability, amount towards future prospects can be awarded.

Thus, notional income comes to Rs. 15,000/- + 40% (Rs. 6,000/-) = 21,000/-.

Thus, income comes to Rs. 21,000/-
per month.
20. The Ex
. P10 Notarized copy of Aadhar card the birth of the year of the petitioner is mentioned as 1996 and the accident occurred in the year of 2021.
Hence, it is clear that as on the date of an accident petitioner was aged 25 years.
As per Sarala Verma's case the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 18.
So future loss of income=( monthly income + future prospects) x 12 months x multiplier x disability, i.e., 21,000x12x18x13%= Rs.5,89,680/-.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled to Rs.5,89,680/- towards loss of future income due to permanent disability.
21. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS AND LOSS OF AMENITIES - To prove what are the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, he has relied on the Ex.P8 is the discharge summary.
By going through discharge summary, it is clear that petitioner has sustained lateral condyle tibia fracture and underwent surgery.

22. In the decision reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 (Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another), the Hon'ble Apex Court made an observation about the general principles relating to compensation in a injury cases.

entities.text: (2011) 1 SCC 343 (Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases.

The provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible,
fully and adeuately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned"
23.
Therefore the duty lies upon this court to award just compensation.
Due to injuries the petitioner has lost the amenities and enjoyment of life.
Thus, he might have been forced to incur amount towards amenities and nutritional food.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, it would be just and reasonable to award an amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- to the petitioner towards Pain and sufferings and loss of amenities of life.

Therefore, an amount of Rs.4,000/- is awarded to the petitioner towards food and nourishment and attendant charges.
25. MEDICAL EXPENSES -
It is the case of the petitioner that he has spent huge money for his treatment.
26. In Ex.P9, petitioner has produced in all 9 medical bills.

The petitioner got reimbursement of Rs.
2,10,613/-.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.44,799/- towards Medical Expenses.

27. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, it might not be possible for him to discharge any work minimum for a period of 2 months.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of income during Laid up period.
28. TRANSPORTATION CHARGES -
The petitioner has taken follow up treatment even after his discharge from the hospital and he has visited the doctor.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded to petitioner towards Transportation charges.
29.FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES -
During the course of cross-examination of PW.3, he has deposed that petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses.

1. Loss of future income due Rs. 5,89,680/-
to permanent disabilities 2. Pain and sufferings & Loss Rs. 1,00,000/-
of amenities.
3. Food and nourishment Rs. 4,000/-
and attendant charges 4.

Medical Expenses Rs. 44,799/-

LIABILITY-
There is no dispute with regard to insurance coverage of the offending vehicle as could be seen from pleadings.
Therefore respondent no.1 being owner of the offending vehicle insured with respondent no.2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
However the primary liability is upon the respondent no.2 to pay the compensation.
In view of the same respondent no.2 has to deposit the compensation amount before the tribunal.
Hence I have answered Point No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:-

32. In view of the discussions made supra, I proceed to pass the following:
:: ORDER ::
The claim petition under Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act filed by the petitioner against respondents is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is awarded total compensation of Rs. 8,13,479/- (Rupees - Eight Lakhs Thirteen Thousand Four Hundred Seventy Nine only) with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of petition till the deposit of the amount in the Tribunal.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent no.2- Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within one month from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount 25% of the share of petitioner, shall be invested in fixed deposit in his name for a period of three years in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice with a liberty to withdraw accrued interest periodically.
The remaining amount shall be released in his favor through e-payment.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
